pencereler.0-5: During the Second World War, some cargo ships suddenly cracked apart. A few suddenly
pencereler.5-12: split completely in two, even at the dock. They were Liberty ships, built fast by welding. In cold water,
pencereler.12-20: their steel turned brittle. Cracks started at sharp corners and weld defects. A welded hull is one piece, so a crack had
pencereler.20-30: nothing to stop it. Metallurgist Constance Tipper showed how the steel failed. Steel toughness then became a basic design requirement.

segmentler.metin: Liberty ships cracked and some broke in two.
It took only welded steel turning brittle in cold seas.
So how could welded steel turning brittle in cold seas do this?
The answer is brittle fracture in welded hulls, starting at sharp corners and weld defects — and it is why Constance Tipper's research made steel toughness a design requirement.
